title: Collective Order Decouples Boundary Selection from Macroscopic Chirality in Confined Active Matter
abstract: Can a boundary determine the direction of circulation in a collectively moving active fluid? We study chiral self-propelled particles with nematic bulk alignment, confined by walls whose orientational coupling varies continuously from nematic to polar. For an isolated particle at a wall, we derive the exact parameter condition under which a stable orientation is tangent to the wall. With predominantly nematic wall coupling, however, the many-body circulation changes sign at a chirality that is nearly independent of the wall symmetry. This sign change follows a pronounced decrease in nematic order and disappears when bulk alignment is removed. As the polar wall coupling becomes dominant, opposite-handed circulation is suppressed and same-handed polar locking emerges. Thus local orientation at a wall and the direction of macroscopic circulation are selected by distinct physical processes: the wall determines the possible local orientations, whereas collective order determines whether those orientations control the global flow.
summary: This paper examines active matter confined by walls whose interaction strength varies continuously. It finds that the direction of global circulation is not solely determined by the wall's anchoring type, but rather by the collective internal order of the particles. This demonstrates a fundamental decoupling between local boundary selection and global transport properties.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the boundary conditions (wall coupling) or the collective internal order of an active fluid dictates the direction of macroscopic circulation.
main_result: The local orientation at the wall and the direction of global circulation are selected by distinct physical processes, meaning the wall only dictates local possibilities, while collective order controls the global flow.
method: The analysis combines theoretical derivations (e.g., single-particle fixed point conditions) with extensive numerical simulations across varying coupling parameters.
model_or_system: The system models chiral self-propelled particles with nematic bulk alignment confined between parallel walls, whose wall coupling strength is continuously tuned between nematic and polar anchoring.
key_observables: Macroscopic chirality (sign of the mean current $\langle J angle$), nematic order parameter ($S$), and the local particle orientation distribution ($p(\psi)$).
important_parameters: The wall coupling parameter $\lambda \in [0, 1]$, which interpolates between nematic ($\lambda=0$) and polar ($\lambda=1$) anchoring.
main_assumptions: The analysis separates the local single-particle dynamics from the many-body collective dynamics, and the comparison between the single-particle fixed point and the many-body sign change is key.
figures_summary: Figures compare the local wall prediction (dashed curve) against the many-body current sign change (solid curve), showing the sign change is independent of $\lambda$ for small $\lambda$ and distinct from the isolated-particle prediction.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's response across different wall coupling regimes ($\lambda$), comparing the local single-particle dynamics to the global many-body current behavior, culminating in the conclusion of decoupling.
why_interesting: The concept of decoupling local boundary effects from global collective behavior is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, active matter, and open quantum systems where boundary conditions play a crucial role.
